cited_by.label: The Amalekite who claimed to kill Saul

precepts.text: Let all things be done decently and in order; the Most High is not the author of vengeance taken out of order.
precepts.point: This is why David is called a man after the Most High's own heart. He did not accept wickedness done in his name or let the murderers slide; he called them out and they received judgment for taking a man's life not ordained of the Lord nor commanded by the king. Let all things be done decently and in order.
precepts.why:
“Let all things be done decently and in order.” Rechab and Baanah slew Ish-bosheth in his own house upon his bed, a man at rest, asleep. It was not even a man-to-man contest for the kingdom. That is not how the Most High brings his purpose to pass, and he is not the author of vengeance taken out of order.

The Most High has his own way of doing things, and his people are not to put the cart before the horse. The kingdom was coming to David, but not by murder done in his name.

So David asked, “shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?” They were slain, their hands and feet cut off, and they were hanged up over the pool in Hebron, while the head of Ish-bosheth was buried in the sepulchre of Abner. They received judgment for taking a man's life that was not ordained of the Lord nor commanded by the king. This is why David is called a man after the Most High's own heart: he did not accept wickedness done in his name or let the murderers slide.

precepts.text: David charged Solomon concerning the blood Joab shed; the doer of evil was rewarded according to his wickedness.
precepts.point: This is why David is called a man after the Most High's own heart. He did not accept wickedness done in his name or let the murderers slide; he called them out and they received judgment for taking a man's life not ordained of the Lord nor commanded by the king. Let all things be done decently and in order.
precepts.why:
David was the same at the end of his life. He charged Solomon concerning Joab: “thou knowest also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, unto Abner the son of Ner, and unto Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace.”

Joab shed blood out of order, in a time of peace, just as Rechab and Baanah slew a righteous person upon his bed. So David said, “Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace.” The doer of evil was rewarded according to his wickedness.

David never let blood shed wickedly slide, not in Ish-bosheth's day and not in Joab's. The same man who slew the messenger in Ziklag, and who hanged Rechab and Baanah over the pool in Hebron, required Joab's blood through his son.

points: When Saul's son Ishbosheth heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble and all the Israelites were troubled.
Ishbosheth had two captains of bands, Baanah and Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite of the children of Benjamin, for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin; and the Beerothites had fled to Gittaim.

Jonathan's son Mephibosheth was lame of his feet. When the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, he was five years old, and his nurse took him up and fled, and in her haste he fell and became lame.
She fled because a new king taking over would customarily kill all the descendants of the former king to make sure none could overthrow him. That is why the nurse ran with the child.

The sons of Rimmon came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who lay on a bed at noon in the hottest part of the day, and came into the midst of the house as though they would fetch wheat, and smote him under the fifth rib.

Rechab and Baanah escaped, having smitten and slain him on his bed; and they beheaded him and took his head and got away through the plain all night, and brought the head to David at Hebron, saying, Behold the head of Ishbosheth thine enemy, and claiming the Lord had avenged the king this day of Saul and his seed.
They did too much; they went overboard. Israel being out of order took the matter upon themselves. David had no quarrel with Saul's sons; it was Saul who sought his life.

David answered Rechab and Baanah that as the Lord liveth, who had redeemed his soul out of all adversity, the man who told him Saul was dead, thinking to bring good tidings, he had taken hold of and slain in Ziklag; that was the reward he gave for such tidings.

This is why David is called a man after the Most High's own heart. He did not accept wickedness done in his name or let the murderers slide; he called them out and they received judgment for taking a man's life not ordained of the Lord nor commanded by the king. Let all things be done decently and in order.

How much more, he said, when wicked men had slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed, should he not require his blood of their hand and take them away from the earth. The man was at rest, asleep, not even a man-to-man contest for the kingdom; it was not how the Most High brings His purpose to pass.

David commanded his young men, and they slew Rechab and Baanah, cut off their hands and feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron, but took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner. The Most High has His own way of doing things; His people are not to put the cart before the horse.
